item.title: Your State's AI Laws: Can Trump Actually Kill Them?
item.description:
This week the White House dropped its National AI Legislative Framework, recommending Congress preempt state AI laws coast to coast. Marcus and James debate whether federal preemption is a competitive necessity or an executive power grab with no teeth — and what it means for the AI stocks in your portfolio.
Timestamps: 00:00 — Cold Open 02:00 — Market Pulse 04:00 — Segment 1 09:00 — Segment 2 16:00 — Segment 3 19:00 — What To Watch

item.title: Your 401k This Week: Why the Fed's Tariff Silence Is Actually Bullish
item.description:
The Fed hasn't called an emergency. Hasn't cut rates out of cycle. Hasn't even flinched. This week Marcus and James debate whether that silence is the most bullish signal of 2026 — or just the calm before a very bad storm. Yale's Budget Lab puts tariff costs at $800 per household. J.P. Morgan sees the effective tariff rate hitting 18-20% by mid-2026. What does any of this mean for your 401k right now?
Timestamps: 00:00 — Cold Open 02:00 — Market Pulse 04:00 — Segment 1 08:00 — Segment 2 15:00 — Segment 3 19:00 — What To Watch
Sources cited in this episode: • Yale Budget Lab (Feb 21, 2026) — Current tariff rate 13.7% (highest since 1941), $1.3T revenue over • Yale Budget Lab — Tariff pass-through to consumers at least 30% for Chinese goods April-December 202 • Yale Budget Lab — Household income loss estimated at $800 annually (short-run, if Section 122 expire • J.P. Morgan (Michael Feroli, Chief U.S. Economist) — Tariffs adding 0.2-0.3% to PCE prices; U.S. eff • J.P. Morgan (Nora Szentivanyi, Senior Global Economist) — Tariff deals (e.g., Vietnam) lifting U.S.
Next episode: If tariff rates hit 18-20% by mid-2026, which sectors get crushed first — and which ones quietly win?
